subject: Pioneer Labs renewal — flexible commit and mid-contract capacity options
messages:
From: Cara Nguyen <cara@pioneerlabs.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + mid-contract growth — need flexible pricing

Hi Evelyn,

Hope you’re well. We’ve accelerated product testing and expect a ~2.3x usage increase over the next 6 months. Our director of ML (cc'd) flagged that the current annual commit will be exhausted ahead of schedule.

Before we enter renewal conversations, two asks from my side:
1) Can Redwood provide a short-term incremental pricing band for mid-contract uplift (3–6 month horizon) that won't require a full year re-commit?
2) If we co-term to calendar year, can you preserve our existing per-token discount band for the remainder of the contract while we annualize new capacity?

We’re evaluating (a) a staged top-up with smoother monthly invoices, or (b) an annualize-now option if the economics are compelling. Budget signoff for 2027 prefers a co-term to Dec 31.

Happy to jump on a quick call; procurement may need a simple amendment template.

Thanks — Cara
Cara Nguyen
Head of Platform
Pioneer Labs

Hi Cara —

Thanks for the heads up and congrats on the ramp — that growth profile tracks with what we’ve seen when customers move from pilot to production. I’ve looped in Ben (sales) and Priyom (rev ops/finance) so we can give you pricing alternatives and a procurement-friendly amendment.

High level we can do both staged top-up and an annualize option; key tradeoffs are:
- Staged top-up: preserves your current commit and pricing bands; incremental usage billed at a blended uplift rate and can be smoothed monthly. Fastest to implement.
- Annualize-now: converts expected uplift into committed units for the remainder of the contract (and gives a deeper discount on incremental units) but requires a short-term co-term amendment.

Ben — can you surface two concrete proposals (numbers + invoicing flow) and attach a simple amendment + SOW stub? Priyom — please call out any billing / revenue recognition impacts we should warn the customer about.

Cara — Can you confirm whether procurement needs PO language, or if DocuSign is fine for an amendment? Also, can you share the estimated uplift in token-hours or USD range so we can price more tightly?

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Pioneer Labs renewal — flexible commit and mid-contract capacity options

Hi Cara — thanks for the context. Attached are two clean options and a short playbook PDF for procurement. Attachments: Pioneer_Renewal_Playbook_v1.pdf, 20260915-pricing-options.csv, Pioneer_SOW_draft.docx

Summary (numbers are illustrative; we can refine once you confirm expected uplift):

Option A — Short-term staged top-up (3–6 months)
- Structure: Add a monthly top-up bucket that is additive to current commit; monthly billing; no long-term re-commit.
- Pricing on incremental usage: +25% over current committed per-token rate for the first 3 months, stepping to +15% for months 4–6 if usage stabilizes.
- Advantages: minimal contract changes (amendment template only), no annualization.
- Implementation lead time: 48 hours to enable buckets.

Option B — Annualize-now, co-term to Dec 31
- Structure: Convert projected uplift into committed units for remainder of current contract and set new co-term to 2026-12-31 (or 2027-12-31 if you prefer a 12-mo).
- Pricing on incremental committed units: 12% discount off current committed per-token rate for the volume converted; additional volume beyond committed units billed at standard overage.
- Billing: Can invoice as a single up-front charge or amortize monthly (we suggest amortization for budget friendliness).
- Advantages: lower marginal unit cost and predictable spend; requires one short amendment and new invoice schedule.

We also propose a limited "growth buffer" safety net: small burst bucket (2x baseline) for emergency spikes with billing at standard overage rates and automatic alerts.

Quick pricing snapshot (example):
- Current committed rate: $0.0009/token
- Option A month 1–3 incremental: $0.001125/token (+25%)
- Option B committed conversion: $0.000792/token (12% discount)

Next steps: confirm estimated uplift band (tokens/month or estimated $/month), whether you want amortized billing, and who in procurement signs (PO vs DocuSign). If you want, I can run a 1-page comparison to show NPV of Option A vs Option B over 12 months.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pioneer Labs renewal — flexible commit and mid-contract capacity options

Thanks Ben — helpful framing. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and finance: 
1) If we pick Option A and later annualize, can we convert prior top-ups to committed units retroactively or is conversion only prospective?
2) For Option B amortized monthly, how does Redwood handle partial period revenue recognition and can you provide an AR-friendly invoice template?
3) Any possible concession on the Option A step (month 4–6) if we add a modest multi-month voucher (we could commit to a small $50k voucher that’s applied against months 4–6)?

Estimated uplift: we expect ~1.8–2.4M tokens/month incremental immediately, ramping to 4–5M tokens/month over 4 months (modeling conservative to aggressive). Budget target for incremental spend is ~$20–$30k/month while we stabilize.

Procurement says DocuSign is acceptable but they will require a PO for any invoice > $50k.

—Cara

-----Original Message-----

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Cara Nguyen <cara@pioneerlabs.com>, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pioneer Labs renewal — flexible commit and mid-contract capacity options

Great detail — thanks. Quick answers: 
1) Conversion policy: conversions from prior top-ups to committed units are allowed but only prospective from the month the conversion is executed; we do not retroactively rebate usage already invoiced. We can, however, apply a one-time voucher credit to earlier months (to cover part of the delta) if agreed in the amendment.

2) Revenue recognition / invoicing: For amortized Option B we can provide a monthly amortization invoice (line item: converted commit amortized over remaining term). Priyom — I’ve attached an AR-friendly invoice template in the Playbook.

3) Voucher concession: we can accept a $50k voucher proposal and pass a partial concession: apply $35k as a month-4 to month-6 bill-credit (pro-rated), and convert $15k towards committed units if you annualize. That preserves revenue visibility while giving you immediate relief for months 4–6.

Refined pricing (using your uplift mid-point ~3M tokens/month):
- Option A (3 months): incremental spend estimate $3,375/month (month 1–3 at +25% rate) — based on 3M tokens * $0.001125 = $3,375.
- Option B (convert to commit, amortized): converted monthly amortization ~$2,376/month (assuming $0.000792/token on converted volume of 3M tokens).

If you want a straight comparison I’ll put NPV over 6 months and 12 months in a 1-pager.

I’ll prepare the amendment + DocuSign envelope; Cara — please confirm signers and whether procurement will add a PO for any >$50k invoice.

Ben
